Use N-mm-MPa units throughout.
Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic behavior and a homogeneous isotropic solid circular shaft, with G = 76923.1 MPa.
The shaft is fixed at x=0 and free at x=L, so it is statically determinate.
The shaft has length L=1200 mm and diameter d=30 mm.
Apply T1=+200000 N·mm at x=L and T2=-200000 N·mm at x=400 mm, with positive torques defined by the right-hand rule.
Compute the fixed-end reaction from global equilibrium: the reaction torque at x=0 is zero.
Segment the shaft into 0 to 400 mm and 400 to 1200 mm.
The internal torque in 0 to 400 mm is zero.
The internal torque in 400 to 1200 mm is +200000 N·mm.
Compute the polar moment of inertia as Ip = pi*d^4/32 = 79521.6 mm^4.
Compute shear stress by tau = T*rho/Ip, with rho measured from the shaft center.
The shear stress in 0 to 400 mm is zero.
The maximum shear stress in 400 to 1200 mm occurs at rho = 15 mm and equals 37.7 MPa.
Compute angle of twist by phi = sum(T_i*L_i/(G*Ip)).
The twist of the segment 0 to 400 mm is zero.
The twist of the segment 400 to 1200 mm is 0.0262 rad.
The total rotation of the free end relative to the fixed end is 0.0262 rad, or 1.50 degrees.
